title: Drop the sun and planets one steel grade

ideaData.title: Drop the sun and planets one steel grade
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): The planetary is currently specified at 20MnCr5 carburised. 16MnCr5 carburised to the same case depth is a cheaper, widely used grade and is what most volume planetary sets in production actually run. The rating changes, so the set has to be re-rated rather than assumed equivalent. SPEC: 16MnCr5 in place of 20MnCr5, case depth held at 0.8-1.5 mm, ISO 6336 rating repeated at 542 N/mm* unit load
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): -£1.30*. SPEC: 16MnCr5 in place of 20MnCr5, case depth held at 0.8-1.5 mm, ISO 6336 rating repeated at 542 N/mm* unit load
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: Re-test: ISO 6336 rating repeated and one rig durability run. No change to wading, articulation or thermal. Trade-off: Lower core strength margin at the V8 rating. If we rate to the gearbox rather than the V8, this idea dies.
ideaData.powertrain: ICE / MHEV (longitudinal I6 ~500 Nm, V8 ~700 Nm, 8AT — study reference vehicle)
ideaData.targetVehicle: SCOPE: two-speed transfer case with lockable centre differential and 2.93:1 low range, for the reference vehicle in A1 (longitudinal I6 ~500 Nm, V8 variant ~700 Nm, 8AT rated 750 Nm INPUT torque, final drive 3.54, 33-in tyres, 3,500 kg braked tow, 900 mm wading, 240,000 km durability, EU plant, >=80,000/yr, 2026 prices). DIRECTIONAL should-cost, not a validated teardown BOM. It ranks effort and tests sensitivity. Every rate below is an input you can argue with — change one and the whole model moves.
ideaData.studyCombinedCapture: COMBINED CAPTURE — honest, and NOT the sum. The saving cards add to roughly £105 and that number is wrong for four reasons. D1 and D2 overlap, because one motor drives both the range change and the clutch today, so taking both saves less than the two figures added together. D1 and D2 are also brand decisions that will most likely be refused in a luxury vehicle, and a refused idea captures nothing. P1, P2 and P3 are supplier savings if we buy the case complete, which we probably will — we capture them through the RFQ, not through our own plant. And D3 is only available if it is taken at the package gate, while D4 depends on a volume split we have not fixed. A realistic engineering-only capture, excluding D1 and D2, is £22-29* gross; net of the protected adders P4 and D5 it is £16-23* on a £355 assembly, roughly 5-7%. Add the actuator RFQ at -25% and it becomes £27-34*. That is the number to commit to, and it is the number this study will be judged on.

title: Induction-harden the chain sprockets instead of carburising them

ideaData.title: Induction-harden the chain sprockets instead of carburising them
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): A gear mesh concentrates load on one or two teeth, so it needs a deep uniform case. A chain spreads load across many links at once, which is why sprockets tolerate a shallower induction case. BorgWarner and Magna both run induction-hardened sprockets in production chain cases. SPEC: induction case in place of carburised case on both sprockets, hardness 55-60 HRC at the flank
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): -£2.16*. SPEC: induction case in place of carburised case on both sprockets, hardness 55-60 HRC at the flank
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: None. The chain path is not affected by wading or articulation. Trade-off: Slightly lower wear margin over 240,000 km of continuous full-time operation. Verify at durability.

title: Do not buy carbon friction plates for the torque-biasing clutch

title: Delete the torque-biasing multiplate clutch and lock the centre differential mechanically

ideaData.title: Delete the torque-biasing multiplate clutch and lock the centre differential mechanically
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): The clutch gives a controllable front/rear bias and a software asset. A dog-clutch lock gives 100% lock and nothing else. INEOS ships the Grenadier this way with a mechanical centre lock usable in both ranges, and still sells it as a serious off-road vehicle. Trade-off: Loses pre-emptive on-road torque bias, which is a refinement and dynamics claim in a luxury vehicle. This is a brand decision with a price, not an engineering decision.

title: Add a front-axle disconnect at the transfer case

ideaData.title: Add a front-axle disconnect at the transfer case
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works (benchmark as named by the study): In full-time 4WD the front path turns continuously and the front hypoid churns oil while carrying almost no torque on tarmac. A disconnect stops that. It is the standard answer on car-derived AWD and is spreading into off-road applications. SPEC: front output disconnect clutch or dog; target measured WLTP driveline loss reduction of 1-2%*, to be confirmed by measurement before the cost is committed
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect (study): +£48* — a cost ADDER assessed against a measured cycle gain. SPEC: front output disconnect clutch or dog; target measured WLTP driveline loss reduction of 1-2%*, to be confirmed by measurement before the cost is committed
ideaData.riskNotes: Duty / environment: Re-validate. Re-engagement behaviour on the trail becomes a new failure mode, and the disconnect must fail engaged, not disengaged. Trade-off: Adds a mechanism and a control path to an assembly whose main virtue is that it always works. Cost it honestly against a measured number, not a modelled one.

title: Resist the gear-drive upgrade until there is a measurement
